work.title: Move to a setup that runs entirely on the local machine
work.goal: Drop the cloud dependencies, have gleanery dashboard draw its screen in the terminal, and read a local SQLite file
work.current: Finished the server side and the screen, and ran them against a local database
next: Human: confirm before deleting the old environment

items.text: Use a single file with Node's built-in node:sqlite. Each machine is independent, with nothing shared between machines
items.context: Looking up the same records across machines is no longer needed. A work machine only needs to hold work records

options.why: users would have to set up Docker and database credentials

items.confirmation: gleanery init applied db/schema.sql, and every DB row in doctor passed
downsides: records do not carry over to a new machine

items.text: Draw the screen in the terminal, with no listening server
items.context: A localhost server can be hit from other pages open in a browser. Opening no port is smaller than keeping a boundary to defend

options.why: it would mean keeping Host checks and CSRF checks forever

items.confirmation: started from outside a terminal, it prints a notice and exits with 1
downsides: images and tables are limited by what the terminal can render

items.text: Capture writes only to the capture views (the authorizer rejects direct writes to base tables)
Dropped pgtyped for typing SQL. It cannot handle search queries whose conditions are built at run time, and its docs state query composition is unsupported
started from a pipe, dashboard prints a notice and exits with 1
Do key input and box lines on the terminal screen hold up on Windows? (No real machine; CI can only check the drawn strings)
